ROUTER SCOPE AMENDMENT to the qa signal filed minutes earlier (pdfocr-orientation-corpus-additional-affected-files-20260825T234250Z.json). That signal is CORRECT in direction but understates scope by ~40x: it names 2 additional files and recommends "a small follow-up FIX/maintenance row". A full corpus scan I ran during return-verification measures 79 FILES / 312 PAGES still carrying pre-fix rotation garble in data/live/market.db pdf_extracted_text. Mint the row at THAT size, not at 2 files.

MEASUREMENT (router, independent, read-only on data/live/market.db; 15887 pages / 372 filenames scanned):
- 79 files, 312 garbled pages, spanning 25 tickers: ACB BID BSR DBC DGC DHG DIG DPM DXG GAS HPG HSG HUT KBC KDC MWG SAB SHB VCI VHM VIC VJC VPB (+ long-form CBTT filenames).
- Worst: VIC_2026_Q2 15/71, VIC_2025_Q4 14/72, KBC_2026_Q2 13/58, GAS-2025-kiem-toan 13/68, KBC_2026_Q1 10/56, KBC_2025_Q4 10/56, KBC.pdf 10/56.
- All affected rows have extracted_at BETWEEN 2026-04-29 AND 2026-08-24 = all pre-orientation-fix. Consistent with a single root cause, already fixed forward by 905e32be1/8d361eee9; this is purely stored-corpus invalidation.

DISCRIMINATOR (calibrated, hand it to whoever builds the sweep so they do not redo this):
  garbled  <=> vietnamese_diacritic_density < 0.10 AND reversed_token_hits >= 3
  Calibration on 4 known-garbled vs 5 known-correct pages gave CLEAN separation with no overlap:
    garbled : density 0.017-0.058, hits 11-72
    correct : density 0.222-0.270, hits 0
  reversed-token regex (case-insensitive, word-bounded):
    Bu[oộôó]p|yeq|Yu[ilr]y|nes|u[eệ]n[yh]u|eno|enuy|Bugp|Budp|Bud[ií]p|Buoyy|jeos|neq|Aex|oyo|uea|Yury|yueop|Budng|Bunp
  Guards that matter: skip pages with <200 alpha chars (short/blank pages are a DIFFERENT defect); str()-coerce text_content (some rows store INTEGER, sqlite is dynamically typed and .isalpha() throws on them).
  KNOWN PRECISION LIMIT, disclosed: 6/6 spot-checked pages were genuinely broken, but 5/6 were orientation garble and 1 (SAB_2026_Q1 p10) was a near-blank total-OCR-miss. The predicate detects "page is broken", slightly broader than "page is rotated". A separate low-diacritic-but-NO-signature population exists (199 files / 1706 pages) that is mostly legitimate English/numeric pages - do NOT sweep that set blind.

COST, AND THE REASON TO CHANGE THE SCRIPT FIRST:
  scripts/migrations/reextract-pdf-ocr-orientation.ts is --filename-scoped and re-extracts EVERY page of a file (it DELETEs by filename then re-inserts all pages). Under that mode the sweep re-OCRs 3786 pages ~= 7.4h @7s/page. Only 312 of those pages are actually broken. Adding an optional --pages <list> (delete+reinsert only the named page_numbers, INSERT OR REPLACE already supports it) cuts the sweep to 312 pages ~= 0.6h, a 12.1x reduction. RECOMMEND: make that script change part of the row, ahead of the sweep - a 7.4h CPU-bound sweep will not fit the pre-market window, a 0.6h one fits comfortably.

SCHEDULING CONSTRAINT: the migration shells pdftoppm+tesseract directly and does NOT route through the pdf-extractor service, so the 02:00-08:59Z pdf-extractor prohibition does not bind it de jure - but a multi-hour CPU-saturating sweep across VN market open is still wrong. Run it in the off-market window.

NOT DONE BY ROUTER, DELIBERATELY: no remediation run, no script edit, no row minted - router is dispatch-only. Detector lives at scratchpad/scan2.py + cost.py for this session only; it is NOT persisted to scripts/ and will be lost, so whoever picks this up should re-home it under scripts/audits/ per dev-standards Script Persistence.
